runes.mechanism: A gift between two sides: something leaves one hand and is received by another, and what arises between them belongs to both and is not counted.
New small life and the care that lets it grow: something fragile begins, and is given room rather than forced.
A word or sound that arrives and changes something: speech heard at the right moment gives a thing its name or its meaning.
Guarding alertness: something watches or stands between a threat and what it protects, open to the world yet letting not everything in.
Value that lives only while it moves: what is used and passed on grows, what is left standing loses its strength.
Time that does the work: what was done long before ripens at its own pace and shows as a result that cannot be hurried.
What is inherited and where one returns: things, ways and places handed down, and the choice of what to carry on.
An uninvited force from outside breaks what looked solid: the plan falls apart, and afterwards it shows what is gone and what held.
The person among people: one sees oneself in or through others, as in a mirror.
A small light that reveals: something that was there all along gets a shape, and once seen it cannot be unseen; a flame that needs feeding.
A direction that costs something: taking one side or keeping one's word and paying the price for it knowingly.
The sharp edge at a threshold: something stops a move just before it is made, and the stop protects or shows what the rush would have missed.
The closed vessel: something exists but is not yet shown or known — not "nothing", but "not yet".
The unmarked: no sign, no name yet — an open space where meaning has not been written.
Standstill: something that was moving has stopped and is held as it is, and in the stillness one thing stays in view.
Ripening inside: from outside nothing seems to happen while something completes itself within, closed until it is ready.
A moment when things fall into place and lighten: shared joy in the middle of things, not a reward for finishing.
Movement made by two: progress that comes only when two find a common rhythm and neither forces the other.
A road made by going: step follows step, a rhythm is found only by moving, and the question is whether the way still leads where one means to go.
The sun's light and strength: it simply shines, and by it one sees where one stands; too bright, it dazzles.
Raw bodily strength that shows only when it is needed: a weight or resistance gives way to a force that was already there.
Holding through change: something bends, stands between two states or endures a long strain, and does not break.
The turn from dark to light: a shift after which the same world looks different and cannot be seen the old way.
Lack and constraint: something is missing or cannot be had, and the pressure shows what is truly needed.
Water and what moves under the surface: something is sensed before it can be explained, or a hidden current finds its own way.

images.image: A gust turns the umbrella inside out, and you push it back into shape.
Your foot moves to the brake before you have named what is wrong.
One person says, "I thought I was the only one," and the table goes quiet.
A drop has frozen at the tip of an icicle, just before it falls.
Two carry a long mirror through the doorway: one pauses, the other turns.
The packed suitcase will not lift until you bend your knees and take its weight.
The phone is at two per cent, and you send the one message that matters.
You refuse the promotion that rests on your colleague's work.
The new flat has one empty wall, and you have not decided what belongs there.
The train is late again, and you two start rating the vending-machine snacks.
The fog lifts, and the trail marker you were walking toward appears.
You turn the map on your phone, and the street falls into place.
You bring a dish to the shared dinner and go home carrying someone else's.
A voice memo is saved as "Untitled", and you cannot recall what you said.
The file downloads overnight while the screen shows nothing happening.
On the long drive you miss your turning because the road was so easy to follow.
The small monthly payments finally cover the cost of the course.
A friend copies the way you tap your foot, and you never knew you did it.
You reach to post the photo, then notice someone in it who never agreed.
A chain of bubbles rises through the dark water, then stops beneath the clear ice.
On the tandem the wobble stops when both riders settle into one pace.
The jar lid will not move until you put your full grip behind it.
After the burst pipe the new ceiling is down, and the old counter still stands.
You tell the referee the ball was out, and your own team loses the point.
The form asks for a detail it never explains, and you leave the box blank.
Halfway through the dishes a song comes on, and you both sing along.
You mute the work chat overnight and leave family calls switched on.
You mend your coat on the sewing machine your mother taught you to use.
The idea comes mid-walk, and you stop to record it before it goes.
A parcel arrives with no sender, and the label gives no clue what is inside.
The dough rests under a tea towel, and by morning it has doubled.
The path across the grass is on no plan; it is where everyone actually walks.
You answer in the new language before you have time to translate the question.
A friend calls you patient, and you have never thought of yourself that way.
You start to interrupt, see the other has not finished, and close your mouth.
The waterfall has become a wall of ice, its last streams held against the rock.
The seedling droops in its new pot, then opens one fresh leaf toward the window.
The bicycle left in the shed all year needs a repair before it will move.
A power cut ends the video call and takes the unsaved slide with it.
Everyone agrees the mistake should be reported, and you put your name on the form.
A new document is open, and the first line is still yours to choose.
You hold the door, and the stranger behind you holds the next one for you.
You share your location with your family and not with the group chat.
The old key still opens the shed at your parents' house.
You change the hallway bulb and see a crack in the ceiling.
The phone case splits when it hits the floor, and the screen beneath is whole.
You keep looking at the same patch of ceiling before any leak appears.
One sentence in the voice message tells you the plan has changed.
The sapling you planted by the bench now shades the place where you sit.
You hear your own phrase come out of a friend's mouth and learn how it sounds.
You have typed the angry reply, and your thumb stops above the send button.
Before the water is shut off you fill one bottle.
The child ties the lace wrong, and your hand stays in your pocket.
The battery you never use is flat on the day you need it.
The flight is cancelled at the gate, and the group chat fills with new plans.
You open the curtains and can finally read the colour on the sample card.
At dawn the street that felt strange in the dark is the one you know.
One friend brings the coffees, and the other has kept a seat.
The door opens on its chain, just far enough to see who is knocking.
You follow your grandmother's recipe card and add the change your family made.
Your phone torch finds the dropped key in the dark under the seat.
The old wooden chair creaks under your weight, bends a little, and holds.
You lower your voice when your friend goes quiet, before either of you knows why.
You say the decision out loud, and it suddenly sounds different.
The lift stops between floors, and everyone inside falls quiet.
Two people work the long saw in turn, and the blade moves cleanly.
The stuck window gives when you lean into the frame with both hands.
One seat is left on the last bus, and it goes to the person on crutches.
The child struggles with the zip, and you wait while they try again.
The food you were saving for a special day is past its date.
The birthday cake leans, and the child asks for the piece sliding off.
After the power cut the apartment block lights up window by window.
One ordinary sentence from its sender makes you read the whole message differently.
The borrowed dish comes back with something baked in it.
The result is ready in the app, but the notification shows no number.
After days of practising alone, the first sentence comes out ready.
A few lengths in, your strokes find a rhythm you no longer count.
